content:
ashley: FYI rack11 has been spiking ECC/Xid errors intermittently for ~36h. Not the usual heat-wave pattern — errors cluster on specific GPUs across multiple nodes.

sandeep: Can you paste dmesg snippets? is it Xid=13 or 79?

ashley: Xid31 and Xid79 mostly, plus a repeated "uncore error" line. sample from node rack11-n4:

```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (31): Ch 00000010, GPU 0: PID 3214: 0x00000006 0x00000000
[ 12346.001234] nvidia: BAR1: uncoupled uncore error detected
[ 12346.001240] NVRM: Xid (79): Ch 00000020, GPU 1: 0x00000004 0x00000000
[ 12346.002345] nvlink: nvlink error: link down on GPU1:port0
```

nora: All affected cards are from vendor lot B-2104, shipped in Jan. Firmware on those nodes is fw-58.1.2 pushed two weeks ago.

devin: Interesting. we saw a similar signature once when a batch had bad uncore silicon + firmware that exposed it under heavy mem write.

ashley: ops metrics show errors surface under long seq lengths + concurrent batches (large prefix caching). Throughput windows 02:00-06:00 UTC correlate with nightly evals.

infra-bot: [ALERT] gpu-health: rack11 6 GPUs with >=3 Xid events in 24h. Autoscaling suggestion: reduce colocated evals.

sandeep: Quick triage checklist I propose:
- collect nvml and dmesg for the 12 affected nodes
- run memtest+gpu-burn on suspect cards (single-GPU, 3hr)
- check nvlink cables and riser seating physically
- verify power supply volt rails on those PSUs
- rollback fw-58.1.2 on a canary card if possible

devin: Commands to run: 
```
for n in rack11-n{1..12}; do ssh $n "sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver --since '48 hours ago' > /tmp/$n-nvidia.log"; scp $n:/tmp/$n-nvidia.log /tmp/diag/; done
sudo gpu-burn -d 0 -t 10800 --memtest
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_uuid,serial,firmware_version,driver_version --format=csv
```

nora: I've already tagged 4 nodes in the inventory with lot=B-2104. serials: [SN-A11, SN-A12, SN-A18, SN-A23]. I'll start collecting logs and open an RMA ticket with vendor citing lot and firmware.

ashley: Impact: 12 GPUs affected across 8 nodes -> estimated capacity loss ~9% on region/cluster. Scheduling drains will push some latency for hosted API customers by ~10-20ms during rebalancing windows. Need customer comms?

ops-oncall: We'll throttle canary drains to off-peak. Plan: tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC drain rack11-n4 and rack11-n7, run gpu-burn on suspect GPU only (pin allocation), if fail -> replace and keep offline for RMA.

devin: If memtest/gpu-burn fails deterministically, capture nvml dump and kernel panic traces, then tag nodes with hardware-failed=true and move to replacement queue. Also export a perfkit trace for the failing time windows.

nora: Vendor asked for logs + serial list. I'll attach the dmesg snippets and list of workloads that triggered it. Also requested expedited RMA for 6 cards.

ashley: Longer-term followups:
- correlate failure rate to firmware fw-58.x across inventory (query inventory DB)
- flag lot B-2104 in procurement to avoid use in QoS-sensitive pools until vendor confirms root cause
- add a health-check that runs periodic mem/stress on a fraction of cards to catch regressions early

sandeep: Agree. Also add a metric to Console showing Xid events per lot_id and firmware_version so ops can pivot routing policies automatically if a cohort spikes.

infra-bot: [ACTION] created ticket INFRA-4729: rack11 cohort ECC/Xid triage. Owner: nora. Due: 2026-03-22.

ashley: Quick note: if we end up rolling back firmware, plan for canary rollback on 2 nodes then monitor for 48h. Rolling back may require driver restart and short downtime.

ops-oncall: Noted. I'll coordinate a 02:00 UTC window and post a dedicated incident thread with customer-facing blurb if we see production impact. :eyes: 

devin: FYI for postmortem template: include timeline (first sighting, firmware push dates), affected serials, stress test results, vendor feedback, capacity impact, mitigation (drain/replace/rollback), and follow-ups (procurement/monitoring).

ashley: I'll own the PM side of the RCA. Nora will own vendor comms and RMA. Sandeep + Devin will do the diagnostic script and monitoring dashboard change. Ops will run the drains.

nora: Started RMA ticket with vendor. attaching initial logs. will update INFRA-4729 as we get vendor reply.

ashley: Thanks all — I'll post summary in #incidents if we confirm widespread cohort issue. For now let's stick to canaries and keep the rest of rack11 in production except the drained nodes.

ops-oncall: Copy. Will post start/finish times before action.
